resources.string: Coordinated beats of motile cilia move mucus along the ciliated respiratory lining. In the nasal cavity, they sweep mucus toward the throat; in the paranasal sinuses, they move it toward the natural openings into the nasal cavity. This example concerns only ciliated respiratory lining, not the outer nose or other nasal linings. A fictional marker advances by the same chosen distance each cycle. The values do not measure or predict real mucus transport.
Marker travel (u) = beat cycles × advance per cycle (u/cycle). Here u is a fictional distance unit; the demo track is 60 u long.
A gold marker shows the distance travelled along the model mucus layer above the blue-green cilia.
